summary.text: Jodi Salvo is a Republican state representative from Ohio House of Representatives District 51 who took office in January 2025 and is seeking re-election on the November 3, 2026 ballot. A social worker and nonprofit director, she is vice chair of the Children and Human Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Salvo was born in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, and earned a bachelor’s degree from California University of Pennsylvania in 1991 and a graduate degree from Marywood University in 1994.
Her career experience includes working as a nonprofit director, medical social worker, home health care social worker and rehabilitation unit case manager.
She has served as president and advisory council member of Ohio’s Statewide Prevention Coalition Association and on Ohio’s Counselor, Social Worker, Marriage & Family Therapist Board.

In a 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Salvo said she had lived in Tuscarawas County for 18 years, was Director of Substance Use Prevention Services at OhioGuidestone and coordinated the Empower Tusc Coalition, and was a licensed master’s-level social worker and Ohio Certified Prevention Consultant.
She won the 2024 Republican primary for District 51 over incumbent Brett Hudson Hillyer and defeated Democrat Joe Rinehart in the general election.
In the 2025–2026 session she serves on the Children and Human Services (vice chair), Community Revitalization, Energy and Natural Resources committees.
